{{Short description|none}} {{Use dmy dates|date=June 2021}} {{Infobox Hurling All-Ireland | year = 1983 | image = | dates = 29 May – 4 September 1983 | teams = 14 | connacht = | munster = Cork | leinster = Kilkenny | ulster = | matches = 14 | poty = [[File:Colours of Kilkenny.svg|15px|border]] [[Frank Cummins (Kilkenny hurler)|Frank Cummins]] | team = Kilkenny | titles = 23rd | captain = [[Liam Fennelly]] | manager = [[Pat Henderson (hurler)|Pat Henderson]] | team2 = Cork | captain2 = [[Jimmy Barry-Murphy]] | manager2 = [[Johnny Clifford]] | totalgoals = | totalpoints = | topscorer = [[File:Colours of Kilkenny.svg|15px|border]] [[Billy Fitzpatrick]] (1–24) | previous = [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship 1982|1982]] | next = [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship 1984|1984]] }} The '''1983 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship''' was the 97th staging of the [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship]], the [[Gaelic Athletic Association]]'s premier [[inter county|inter-county]] [[hurling]] tournament. The championship ran from 29 May to 4 September 1983. [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]] were the [[1982 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|defending champions]].{{cite news|url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/2009/0622/250735-1982hurling/|title=GAA 125 - 1982 All-Ireland Hurling Final|publisher=RTÉ Sport|date=22 June 2009|accessdate=30 July 2026|first=|last=}}{{cite news|url=https://www.echolive.ie/corksport/arid-41185993.html|title=All-Ireland SHC final: History not necessarily on Limerick's side - but they're good at bucking trends|publisher=Echo Live|date=20 July 2023|accessdate=30 July 2026|first=|last=}} The [[1983 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final|All-Ireland final]] was played on 4 September 1983 at [[Croke Park]] in [[Dublin]], between Kilkenny and [[Cork GAA|Cork]], in what was their second consecutive meeting in the All-Ireland final.{{cite news|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaa/hurling/cork-v-kilkenny-the-facts/a/147825136.html|title=Cork v Kilkenny: The facts|publisher=Irish Independent|date=9 August 2008|accessdate=30 July 2026|first=|last=}} Kilkenny won the match by 2–14 to 2–12 to claim their 23rd All-Ireland title overall and a second consecutive title.{{cite news|url=https://www.kilkennypeople.ie/community/pictures-forty-years-on-kilkenny-prepares-to-relive-the-double-double-7413279|title=PICTURES: Forty years on - Kilkenny prepares to relive the double-double!|publisher=Kilkenny Live|date=23 June 2023|accessdate=30 July 2026|first=|last=}}{{cite news|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-30936399.html|title=How fickle hand of fortune changed the course of Cork-Kilkenny history|publisher=Irish Examiner|date=12 July 2019|accessdate=30 July 2026|first=|last=}}{{cite news|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaa/hurling/kilkenny-are-the-supreme-champions/a/149702522.html|title=Kilkenny are the supreme champions|publisher=Irish Independent|date=14 March 2001|accessdate=30 July 2026|first=|last=}} Kilkenny's [[Billy Fitzpatrick]] was the championship's [[#Top scorers|top scorer]] with 1–24. Kilkenny's [[Frank Cummins (Kilkenny hurler)|Frank Cummins]] was the choice for [[Texaco Hurler of the Year|Hurler of the Year]].{{cite news|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-20114611.html|title=Worldly Cummins has parish pride|publisher=Irish Examiner|date=16 March 2010|accessdate=30 July 2026|first=|last=}} == Team Hurling Championship|Leinster]] were all played on a knock-out basis as usual. In keeping with the rotation system for advancement to the All-Ireland final, the Leinster champions automatically qualified for the final of 1983. [[Galway GAA|Galway]], having no competition in the [[Connacht Senior Hurling Championship|Connacht Championship]], played the winners of a preliminary game between [[Kerry GAA|Kerry]] and [[Antrim GAA|Antrim]]. Goalkeeper [[Noel Skehan]] won a record-breaking ninth All-Ireland medal, however, his first three were won as non-playing substitutes. Midfielder [[Frank Cummins (Kilkenny hurler)|Frank Cummins]] won his seventh All-Ireland medal on the field of play, equalling the record of four other Kilkenny players from the early part of the century. It was his eighth winners' medal overall as he won a non-playing substitutes' medal in 1967.
